decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Paste a web address… optional tags.” R1 client did not contest URL saving or tag assignment.
decisions.note: The baseline save-and-tag behavior conforms at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker limited saving to “a title (auto-derived if you don't give one)” and assumption 4 said “reference + title only.” R1 client: “collect the page title, description, icon, and preview image automatically” and allow title/description changes before and after saving.
decisions.note: The client replaced the limited metadata/editing decision with the reference-conforming behavior at the first specification review.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker offered editing only “titles and tags.” R1 client requested editing “the address, title, description, tags, and a longer note.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing editable fields at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no note feature. R1 client requested “a longer note” whose basic formatting is displayed when viewed.
decisions.note: The response caught the omitted formatted-note capability, although it did not yet establish the Markdown representation.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker only said “See all saved bookmarks.” R1 client specified that the list show “title, description, tags, and page icon.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing per-item readability fields.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker did not specify list-item navigation. R1 client: “selecting a bookmark should open the original page.”
decisions.note: The original-URL navigation behavior was missing and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker limited keyword search to “title, address, and tags.” R1 client required search over “titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the full-text field coverage.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker did not define case handling. R1 client: “Search should ignore letter case.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive matching was supplied as a missing search rule.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker only mentioned generic keyword/tag filtering. R1 client requested “tag searches such as `#travel`.”
decisions.note: The client added the required hash-tag query syntax.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker specified no Boolean grammar. R1 client requested “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: The missing Boolean and grouping behavior was caught at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker specified only keyword search. R1 client requested “exact phrases in quotation marks.”
decisions.note: Exact-phrase search was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “filter by tag.” R1 client did not dispute this behavior.
decisions.note: Filtering to a tag's bookmarks conforms at the initial specification stage.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker allowed tags but offered no entry suggestions. R1 client: “suggestions from tags I have already used.”
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete was an omitted related requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: “Warns on duplicate addresses.” R1 client: “should not merely warn me; it should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, without creating a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The client replaced warning-only behavior with convergence on the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no read-later workflow. R1 client requested a read-later state, separate unread view, and a way to mark items read.
decisions.note: The complete unread/read-later workflow was missing and explicitly supplied.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker included deletion but no archive. R1 client required archiving “as well as deletion,” exclusion from normal list/search, a separate archive view, and restoration.
decisions.note: The response added reversible archiving and distinguished it from deletion.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no multi-selection actions. R1 client requested selecting multiple bookmarks and changing tags, read status, archive status, or deleting them together.
decisions.note: The omitted selected-item bulk actions were caught.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no whole-result action. R1 client: “apply those actions to everything matching my current search or filter.”
decisions.note: The filter-scoped whole-collection action was explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented an unsorted browse list. R1 client: “sorting, such as by date added or title.”
decisions.note: The missing sort behavior was added.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no reusable filter entity. R1 client wanted to save combinations of searches and included or excluded tags.
decisions.note: The client added the bundle/saved-filter requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker assumption 5: “No browser import/export in v1.” R1 client: “I do want import and export using the usual browser bookmark file format, preserving titles, tags, and dates.”
decisions.note: The client directly reversed the exclusion of import/export.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker assumption 4 said the app “does not archive full page contents.” R1 client requested a local page copy, “with PDFs saved as PDFs.”
decisions.note: The explicit exclusion of local preservation was corrected.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker offered no external snapshot function. R1 client requested optionally saving a copy through the Internet Archive.
decisions.note: The Internet Archive capability was added as a missing requirement.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented no personal display settings. R1 client requested default sorting, displayed-item count, and text size.
decisions.note: Display preferences were omitted and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker included deletion with confirmation. R1 client retained deletion while requesting archive as an additional operation.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion itself conforms; the separately missing archive behavior is classified above.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: metadata includes “title/description/icon/preview auto-collected; editable before & after.” R2 client called the revision “very close” and did not contest this decision.
decisions.note: The revised metadata and edit timing conform.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “no duplicates — opens the existing bookmark for editing.” R2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: list shows title/description/tags/icon, sorts by date/title, and opens the original URL. R2 client raised no objection.
decisions.note: The revised browse, open, and sort decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker described case-insensitive search over title/description/note/address, `#tag`, and quoted phrases. R2 client retained these features.
decisions.note: These revised search capabilities conform; two omitted search-composition rules are separate decisions below.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker listed text and `#tag` search but did not state their conjunction rule. R2 client: “a tag term and an ordinary text term together should both have to match.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing implicit-AND rule at the second specification review.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker listed AND/OR/NOT and parentheses but omitted the literal-operator rule. R2 client required those words to be ordinary text “only when I put them in quotation marks.”
decisions.note: The quoted-literal edge rule was caught before approval.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: edit address/title/description/tags/note and provide tag suggestions. R2 client did not contest these behaviors.
decisions.note: The revised field editing and autocomplete decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker defined “basic formatting” as bold, italic, lists, and links, with unsupported formatting dropped. R2 client said this proposal was “fine,” but neither entry established whether notes were authored and stored as Markdown.
decisions.note: At this specification-stage decision, the observable record cannot establish conformity or divergence from the Markdown requirement. The later plan makes a concrete HTML decision, classified separately.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker default: “New bookmarks default to unread.” R2 client: “They should be ordinary bookmarks unless I choose ‘read later’… or mark them unread afterward.”
decisions.note: The client replaced an automatic unread default with an explicit read-later choice.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker retained a dedicated unread view and marking items read. R2 client corrected only the default state.
decisions.note: The unread view and mark-read behaviors conform.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker described archive hiding from normal list/search, restoration, and separate confirmed deletion. R2 client raised no objection.
decisions.note: The revised archive/delete lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker listed bulk “tags/read/archive/delete” without tag-delta semantics. R2 client required explicit add/remove operations that do not replace unrelated tags.
decisions.note: The client corrected the underspecified bulk-tag behavior.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker included multi-select or “all matching” bulk scope. R2 client retained that scope.
decisions.note: Filter-scoped whole-result bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “named query + included/excluded tag sets.” R2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: The saved-filter/bundle decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker chose Netscape bookmark HTML preserving titles, tags, and dates. R2 client explicitly said the Netscape HTML format was “fine.”
decisions.note: This is a conforming format decision, not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker promised an “offline copy” and PDF handling but did not specify the required single-file HTML form. R2 client: “A preserved web page should be stored as a self-contained HTML file. A PDF should remain a PDF.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the required preservation format.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker included optional Internet Archive saving. R2 client did not contest it.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker included default sort, items per view, and text size. R2 client did not contest them.
decisions.note: The display-preference decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: new bookmarks are ordinary/read by default and become unread only by user choice. R3 client: “these corrections match what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The corrected read-later default conforms at final specification approval.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: web pages use “a single self-contained HTML file” and PDFs remain PDFs. R3 client approved the corrections.
decisions.note: The corrected local-snapshot format conforms.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker: bulk operations add or remove specific tags “without replacing” other tags. R3 client approved.
decisions.note: The corrected bulk-tag delta semantics conform.

decisions.evidence: R3 maker made adjacent terms implicit AND and operators literal when quoted. R3 client approved the corrections.
decisions.note: The corrected search-composition rules conform.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker planned server-side title/description/OpenGraph/favicon collection with fallbacks. R4 client said the plan covered the approved behavior.
decisions.note: The metadata design conforms at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker planned canonical-address duplicate handling. R4 client approved the plan.
decisions.note: The duplicate-handling plan fulfills the reference requirement; additional normalization choices are outside the one-way reference test.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker planned a parser supporting implicit AND, tag/text conjunction, quoted literal operators, precedence, phrases, and malformed-query errors. R4 client explicitly cited the corrected search rules in approving the plan.
decisions.note: The search design conforms at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker chose “`contenteditable` toolbar → HTML sanitised to an allow-list.” R4 client generally approved the plan but did not state the reference expectation of a Markdown note or identify the HTML departure.
decisions.note: The concrete plan uses authored/stored HTML rather than Markdown. The broad approval does not qualify as an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker planned self-contained HTML, PDFs stored as PDF, and optional Internet Archive submission. R4 client specifically approved the preservation approach.
decisions.note: The preservation design conforms.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker planned Netscape HTML import/export preserving titles, tags, and dates. R4 client approved the plan.
decisions.note: The import/export design conforms.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker described independent unread/archive flags, read-by-default, bulk add/remove deltas, IDs-or-current-match scope, saved searches, and preferences. R4 client approved these corrected behaviors.
decisions.note: These data-model and API behavior decisions conform at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker presented 56 tasks across all 15 phases and all 12 approved stories. R5 client approved but required the P1 MVP to be only an internal checkpoint and “all 15 phases and all 12 approved user stories” to be delivered.
decisions.note: The task-breakdown scope already covered the full reference feature set; the client clarified delivery timing rather than correcting a stated plan to stop after P1. The separate HTML-note mechanism remains classified at the plan and implementation decisions.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported URL saving, auto-collected title/description/icon/preview, and editing before/after. R6 client accepted all 12 stories.
decisions.note: The presented save/metadata implementation conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported that re-saving a normalized variant opens the existing bookmark. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported list fields, date/title sorting, and opening the original URL. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented browse, navigation, and sort behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported case-insensitive search, `#tag`, phrases, implicit AND, quoted literal operators, precedence, and malformed-query handling. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented search implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported editing all fields, tag suggestions, and collision prevention. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented bookmark editing and tagging behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported “sanitised formatted notes (scripts stripped),” implementing the R4 contenteditable/HTML design. R6 client said all stories matched and accepted, but did not identify the difference from Markdown notes.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the note feature remains HTML-based rather than Markdown; bare overall approval does not establish awareness or accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported ordinary-by-default bookmarks, explicit unread choice, and a dedicated unread view. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented read-later workflow conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported reversible archive hidden from normal list/search and confirmed deletion. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented archive/delete lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported selection or all-matching bulk scope and tag add/remove deltas preserving other tags. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented bulk-action behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported named queries with included/excluded tags and apply/rename/delete operations. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented bundle/saved-search behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported Netscape import/export preserving titles, tags, and dates. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented import/export implementation conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported self-contained HTML, PDFs retained as PDF, and optional Internet Archive saving. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented preservation behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker reported persisted default sort, items per view, and text size. R6 client accepted the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented personal display settings conform.
